quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your risk of a crash?

options.text: Do not use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Look about five feet ahead of your motorcycle while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to communicate. Keep space around your motorcycle and scan ahead, behind, and beside your vehicle. Always be ready to avoid an unexpected hazard.

questions.question: Proper riding clothing provides all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothing protects you from injury in a crash. It also protects you from weather and other hazards. Good clothing should add comfort, not discomfort.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can your body eliminate per hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. The time it takes to lower your blood alcohol content varies. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from the cars. This protects you from doors opening or people stepping out. This also gives you more room to react to hazards.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Your entire face, not just your eyes.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your entire face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Rely only on your mirrors to see all traffic.
Point in the direction you are changing lanes.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: How much stopping power does the front brake provide?
questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which of the following should a passenger never do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: Passengers should always ride facing forward. In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All passengers should wear tight clothing to prevent it from catching on the motorcycle and should lean with the rider when turning.

questions.question: Why should riders in a group avoid riding in pairs?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections may make it hard for riders to see.
Riding in pairs does not allow enough space to maneuver.
It is too difficult for left-side riders to exit a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not allow enough space to maneuver.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should not ride side by side. Neither rider will have enough room to maneuver and avoid hazards.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Keep other drivers from knowing what you plan to do.
Always stay very close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show what you plan to do. Keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: How should you control your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Keep the motorcycle straight without leaning.
Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle through a turn, look ahead through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn or change lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes to see if other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light when:

options.text: You will slow down where drivers don't expect it.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will slow down where drivers don't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than larger vehicles' brake lights. Flash your brake light to warn drivers before you slow down unexpectedly, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, do these actions separately—not at the same time. You can brake then swerve, or swerve then brake.

questions.question: To stop other vehicles from sharing your lane, you should ride:

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
In the center of your lane.
In a zigzag pattern to fill the lane.
In a zigzag pattern to fill the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, be ready for:

options.text: A parked car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
Other drivers to see you and stay out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for a car to pull out suddenly. Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right to give yourself more space between your motorcycle and the parked vehicles.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees they will let you go.
Does not mean they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that a driver will yield to you just because they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but still don't notice them.

questions.question: On a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine if you feel sleepy.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to stay alert.
questions.explanation: On a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours a day and take a rest break every two hours. Avoid caffeine and stimulants because you will crash when they wear off.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.
